mainTopic: Whose view is the משנה's rule that only a robber who swore falsely must make sure the real owner gets paid: רבי עקיבא or רבי טרפון, in light of their מחלוקת about robbing one of five people?
overview: The amud opens with the end of the משנה. A robber who swears falsely about the extra חומש must add a new חומש on top of it, again and again, until the amount drops below a פרוטה. The same rule of קרן, חומש and אשם applies to a פקדון and the other cases in the פסוק. The גמרא notes that the משנה makes the robber chase the victim only if he swore. It asks whose view that is, using the מחלוקת of רבי טרפון and רבי עקיבא about someone who robbed one of five people. First it answers that the משנה follows רבי עקיבא, who is strict only after an oath. It explains רבי טרפון's leniency through the enactment of paying the בית דין. רב הונא בר יהודה and רבא knock down this answer, with a ברייתא about a buyer and a story about a חסיד. So the גמרא switches: the משנה follows רבי טרפון, who agrees to be strict after an oath because of the פסוק, while רבי עקיבא is strict even without an oath as a קנס. Finally the גמרא asks why the משנה needs the oath at all, since רבי טרפון is strict whenever the robber admits on his own. It begins quoting a ברייתא that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A fifth on top of a fifth
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that if the robber swears falsely about the חומש itself, he pays a new חומש on it. This repeats until the amount is less than a פרוטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: This robber pays a fifth on top of a fifth, until the principal drops below the value of a פרוטה.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes its rule. If someone swears falsely about the extra חומש he owes, that חומש now counts like a new קרן, and he must add another חומש to it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The false oath is what creates the חומש obligation. So each new false oath about a leftover חומש creates a fresh חומש. The chain only stops when the amount he denied is worth less than a פרוטה, because below a פרוטה there is no real money claim.

keyTerms.meaning: The extra fifth added as a penalty for a false oath
The principal, meaning the base amount owed
The smallest coin that counts as real money in הלכה

phrases.aramaic: הֲרֵי זֶה מְשַׁלֵּם חוֹמֶשׁ עַל חוֹמֶשׁ,
phrases.english: this one pays a fifth on top of a fifth,
until the principal is reduced to less than the value of a perutah.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲרֵי זֶה מְשַׁלֵּם חוֹמֶשׁ עַל חוֹמֶשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה from the previous daf about a robber who swore falsely.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A false oath about a חומש creates a new חומש, repeating until the amount is under a פרוטה.

steps.title: The same rule applies to a deposit
steps.stepSummary: The משנה extends the rule to a פקדון and the other cases in the פסוק. Whoever denies them and swears falsely pays קרן, חומש, and brings an אשם.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the same is true with a deposit, as it says: 'with a deposit, or a pledge, or robbery, or he exploited his fellow, or he found a lost item, and denied it and swore falsely.' This person pays the principal, a fifth, and brings a guilt-offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה says the rules it taught about גזל also apply to someone who denies a פקדון. It quotes the פסוק that lists all these cases together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק puts פקדון, a pledge, גזל, withholding wages, and a lost item in one list. That tells us they all share the same consequence for a false oath. The consequence has three parts: return the קרן, add a חומש, and bring a קרבן אשם.

keyTerms.meaning: A deposit, something left with someone for safekeeping
A pledge or loan entrusted into someone's hand

steps.whatToRemember: A false oath denying money owed (גזל, פקדון, a lost item and the rest) means paying קרן, plus חומש, plus bringing a קרבן אשם.

phrases.english: And so too with a deposit, as it is stated:
"with regard to a deposit, or with regard to a pledge,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ בְגָזֵל, אוֹ עָשַׁק אֶת עֲמִיתוֹ
phrases.english: or with regard to a robbery, or if he exploited his fellow,
or he found a lost item;
and he denied it and swore falsely" —

phrases.aramaic: הֲרֵי זֶה מְשַׁלֵּם קֶרֶן וָחוֹמֶשׁ וְאָשָׁם.
phrases.english: this one pays the principal, and a fifth, and brings a guilt-offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵן בְּפִקָּדוֹן, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the משנה's rules from גזל to פקדון and the other cases in the פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Anyone who denies a פקדון or similar and swears falsely pays קרן, חומש, and brings an אשם.

steps.title: Whose view is the rule about the oath?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא infers that only a robber who swore must go to great lengths to return the item. It then asks whose view this is, since it fits neither רבי טרפון nor רבי עקיבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: If he swore to him, yes; if he did not swear to him, no. Whose view is this? It is neither רבי טרפון nor רבי עקיבא!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads the משנה closely. Only someone who swore falsely has to chase the victim, even all the way to מדי. Then it challenges this: no known תנא seems to hold that way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The inference creates a split. With an oath, he has full responsibility to get the item into the victim's hands. Without an oath, he does not. The גמרא claims that neither side of the coming מחלוקת allows this split, so it is setting up a source to prove its point.

phrases.english: Gemara
If he swore to him — yes,
phrases.notes: Yes, he has to go after the victim to give it back, even all the way to מדי, like the משנה said.

phrases.english: if he did not swear to him — no;
Whose view is this?

phrases.aramaic: לָא רַבִּי טַרְפוֹן וְלָא רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא!
phrases.english: Not רבי טרפון and not רבי עקיבא!

steps.triggerLanguage: נִשְׁבַּע לוֹ – אִין, לֹא נִשְׁבַּע לוֹ – לָא; מַנִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא by inferring a rule from the משנה about the oath requirement.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's implied rule that the duty to chase the victim depends on a false oath.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Neither רבי טרפון nor רבי עקיבא makes the robber's duty depend on whether he swore.

steps.title: The case of robbing one of five people
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the מחלוקת between רבי טרפון and רבי עקיבא about a robber who doesn't know which of five people he robbed.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught: If someone robbed one of five people and does not know which one, and each says 'He robbed me,' he places the stolen item among them and leaves. These are the words of רבי טרפון. רבי עקיבא says: This is not the way to free him from the sin. He must pay the stolen item to each and every one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source behind its challenge. It is a disagreement about how far a robber must go when he is unsure who the victim is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי טרפון is lenient. Leaving the item with the group is enough, even though it may not reach the real owner. רבי עקיבא is strict. He must pay each of the five in full, so that the real victim surely gets his money back.

keyTerms.meaning: He leaves the stolen item among them

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix them up: רבי טרפון is the lenient one (leave it among them), and רבי עקיבא is the strict one (pay everyone).

phrases.english: As it is taught:
If he robbed one of five people
and he does not know which of them,
and each one says: "He robbed me" —
he places the stolen item among them and withdraws,
these are the words of רבי טרפון.
רבי עקיבא says:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא זוֹ דֶּרֶךְ מוֹצִיאָתוֹ מִידֵי עֲבֵירָה,
phrases.english: This is not the way that frees him from the sin,
until he pays the stolen item to each and every one.
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is added in the corrected wording.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא: גָּזַל אֶחָד מֵחֲמִשָּׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for the claim that neither Tanna fits the משנה.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that the משנה matches neither רבי טרפון nor רבי עקיבא.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא (also in יבמות) on robbing one of five people.

steps.title: Why neither Tanna fits the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא spells out the problem. רבי טרפון is lenient even when there was an oath, and רבי עקיבא is strict even when there was no oath.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is it? If רבי טרפון: even though he swore, he says he leaves the item among them and goes. If רבי עקיבא: even though he did not swear, he says he must pay each and every one!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows exactly why the משנה clashes with each תנא. It sharpens the question it asked in step 3.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה makes the oath the deciding factor. But רבי טרפון stays lenient even with an oath, so he cannot be the source of the משנה's strict rule. רבי עקיבא is strict even without an oath, so he cannot be the source of the משנה's leniency when there was no oath.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the גמרא's coming answer. It will need to explain the משנה in a way that fits one of these תנאים.

phrases.english: Whose view is it?
If רבי טרפון —
even though he swore, he says:
he places the stolen item among them and withdraws!
If רבי עקיבא —

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּלָא אִישְׁתְּבַע, אָמַר:
phrases.english: even though he did not swear, he says:

phrases.aramaic: עַד שֶׁיְּשַׁלֵּם גְּזֵילָה לְכׇל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד!
phrases.english: he must pay the stolen item to each and every one!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַנִּי? אִי רַבִּי טַרְפוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the ברייתא to the משנה, explaining the challenge from step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: Attributing the משנה's oath-based distinction to either רבי טרפון or רבי עקיבא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי טרפון is lenient even with an oath. רבי עקיבא is strict even without one. Neither makes the oath decide the outcome.

steps.title: The משנה follows רבי עקיבא, who is strict only when the robber swore
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה is רבי עקיבא's view. His strict ruling, that the robber must pay each of the five people, applies only when the robber swore falsely. The source is the פסוק "לאשר הוא לו יתננו ביום אשמתו".
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, the משנה is רבי עקיבא. When רבי עקיבא says the robber must pay every one of the five, he is talking about a robber who swore. Why? Because the פסוק says, "To the one it belongs to, he must give it, on the day of his guilt."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the problem from Step 5. It says the משנה matches רבי עקיבא after all, because his strictness only covers a robber who swore falsely.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 5, the problem was that רבי עקיבא seemed strict even without an oath. The גמרא now limits his ruling: he only requires paying all five people when there was a false שבועה. The פסוק about returning the item 'to whom it belongs' appears in the section about a false oath, so the extra effort is tied to swearing.

keyTerms.meaning: Really / actually. It signals that the גמרא is holding on to its first idea and explaining it.
"To the one it belongs to, he must give it." This is the פסוק that requires the swearer to return the item to its real owner.

steps.whyThisMatters: This answer makes רבי עקיבא's whole strict view depend on the oath. Everything that follows in this section tests whether that limit holds up.

phrases.english: Really, it is Rabbi Akiva,
and when Rabbi Akiva says

phrases.aramaic: עַד שֶׁיְּשַׁלֵּם גְּזֵילָה לְכׇל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד –
phrases.english: "until he pays the stolen item to each and every one"
it is where he swore that he says it.
What is the reason?
Because the verse says:
"To the one it belongs to, he shall give it, on the day of his guilt."

steps.triggerLanguage: לְעוֹלָם רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the problem raised in Step 5 by limiting רבי עקיבא's ruling to a robber who swore.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of an opinion: רבי עקיבא's strictness applies only to a robber who swore.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought רבי עקיבא required paying all five people even without an oath, so he could not match the משנה.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי עקיבא is strict only when there was a false oath, based on the פסוק, so the משנה fits him.

steps.title: Why רבי טרפון is lenient even after an oath
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רבי טרפון can be lenient when the robber swore, since the פסוק seems to require full return. It answers that the רבנן made an enactment that applies even after an oath.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי טרפון? Even though the robber swore, the רבנן made an enactment.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now explains רבי טרפון. Even with an oath, he can be lenient because the רבנן made a special enactment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By Torah law, a robber who swore should have to return the item to its true owner. רבי טרפון still lets him put the money down among the five people and leave. That is because a rabbinic enactment eases the burden in this kind of situation. The source of the enactment comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: The רבנן made an enactment (a rabbinic rule to help in a hard situation).

phrases.english: And Rabbi Tarfon?
phrases.notes: The question isn't said out loud: how can he be lenient if the פסוק says to give it back to the owner?

phrases.english: Even though he swore,
the Rabbis made an enactment.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי טַרְפוֹן אַף עַל גַּב דְּאִישְׁתְּבַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After setting the Torah rule for a robber who swore, the גמרא explains how רבי טרפון can still be lenient.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי טרפון's leniency in a case where the robber swore.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק requires a robber who swore to return the item to its owner, so how can רבי טרפון let him simply put the money down and leave?
steps.terutzResolutionType: A rabbinic enactment that eases the Torah requirement.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: After an oath, the robber would have to pay all five people.
steps.terutzMaskana: The רבנן made an enactment that lets him off even after an oath.

steps.title: The source: the great enactment of רבי אלעזר ברבי צדוק
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא. If returning the item costs more than the item itself, the robber may pay the קרן and חומש to the בית דין, bring his אשם, and gain atonement.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: רבי אלעזר ברבי צדוק says, they made a great enactment. If the cost of returning it is more than the קרן, he pays the קרן and חומש to the בית דין, brings his אשם, and is forgiven.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings proof that the enactment from Step 7 really exists. It quotes the ברייתא of רבי אלעזר ברבי צדוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a robber must bring the money to the owner himself, even if it is hard. The enactment says that if the expense is more than the stolen amount, he may give it to the בית דין instead and still complete his atonement. Paying all five people costs more than the קרן, so רבי טרפון applies this enactment to our case.

keyTerms.meaning: An expense that is more than the קרן (the stolen amount).

phrases.english: As it was taught in a ברייתא:
Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Tzadok says:
They enacted a great enactment:

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאִם הָיְתָה הוֹצָאָה יְתֵירָה עַל הַקֶּרֶן –
phrases.english: that if the expense was more than the principal,
he pays the principal and the fifth to the court,
and brings his guilt-offering and is granted atonement.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי צָדוֹק אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the enactment mentioned in Step 7.
steps.raayaObject: That the רבנן made an enactment that frees a robber who swore from bringing the money to the owner himself.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of רבי אלעזר ברבי צדוק about paying the בית דין when the expense is more than the קרן.

steps.title: Why רבי עקיבא does not use this enactment for one of five
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that according to רבי עקיבא, the enactment only applies when the robber knows whom he robbed, because then the money really reaches the owner. When he robbed one of five and doesn't know which, the money doesn't reach the owner, so there is no enactment.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי עקיבא? The רבנן made the enactment only where he knows whom he robbed, since then the money goes back to its owner. But if he robbed one of five and doesn't know whom, the money doesn't go back to its owner, so the רבנן made no enactment.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבי עקיבא does not accept the enactment in the one-of-five case. The enactment only works when the money actually gets back to the owner.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the enactment's case, the בית דין knows who the owner is and passes the money to him. In the one-of-five case, putting the money down among them does not guarantee it reaches the right person. So according to רבי עקיבא, the enactment does not apply there.

keyTerms.meaning: He returns the money to its owner.

steps.whatToRemember: Summary of this first answer, which steps 10-15 challenge and step 16 replaces: the משנה follows רבי עקיבא, who is strict only after an oath, based on the פסוק. רבי טרפון relies on the enactment of paying the בית דין. רבי עקיבא limits that enactment to a case where the owner is known.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Akiva?
when the Rabbis made the enactment,
it was where he knows whom he robbed,
since he is returning the money to its owner;
but one who robbed one of five,
where he does not know whom he robbed,
where the money does not go back to its owner —
the Rabbis did not make an enactment.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא כִּי עֲבוּד רַבָּנַן תַּקַּנְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After grounding רבי טרפון's view in the enactment, the גמרא explains why רבי עקיבא does not apply it to the one-of-five case.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי עקיבא's refusal to use the enactment.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the enactment exists, why doesn't רבי עקיבא also let the robber put the money down and leave?
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the enactment's scope to cases where the owner is known.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The enactment should apply in every case where returning the money is costly.
steps.terutzMaskana: The enactment applies only when the money actually reaches its owner, which does not happen in the one-of-five case.

steps.title: רב הונא בר יהודה's challenge: both agree about a buyer
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בר יהודה challenges the answer with a ברייתא. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says that רבי טרפון and רבי עקיבא agree about a buyer who doesn't know which of five people he bought from. He puts the money among them and leaves.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא בר יהודה challenged: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר said, רבי טרפון and רבי עקיבא did not disagree about someone who bought from one of five people and doesn't know which one. He puts the purchase money among them and leaves.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא בר יהודה opens a challenge to the answer that רבי עקיבא is strict only after an oath. This step sets up the challenge by quoting the first half of a ברייתא about a buyer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says both תנאים agree that a buyer may leave the money among them. They argue only about a robber. That split between buying and robbing will be the basis of the challenge to Step 6, which is spelled out in Step 12.

keyTerms.meaning: He places the purchase money among them.
He leaves (he is done with his obligation).

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two cases. Here it is a buyer (לקח), who did nothing wrong. Only in the next step does the ברייתא turn to the robber (גזל).

phrases.english: Rav Huna bar Yehuda raised an objection:
Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar said:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא נֶחְלְקוּ רַבִּי טַרְפוֹן וְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
phrases.english: Rabbi Tarfon and Rabbi Akiva did not disagree
about one who bought from one of five
and does not know from which of them he bought —
that he places the purchase money among them and leaves.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵתִיב רַב הוּנָא בַּר יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new challenge against the answer given in Step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer from Step 6 that רבי עקיבא is strict only when the robber swore.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא makes רבי עקיבא's strictness depend on robbing as opposed to buying. If the oath were what mattered, buying or robbing would make no difference. The full argument comes in Step 12.

steps.title: The ברייתא continues: where they disagree is about a robber
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says the disagreement is only about a robber who doesn't know which of five people he robbed. רבי טרפון says he puts the money among them and leaves. רבי עקיבא says he has no fix until he pays every one of them.
steps.simpleTranslation: About what did they disagree? About someone who robbed one of five people and doesn't know which. רבי טרפון says he puts the value of the stolen item among them and leaves. רבי עקיבא says he has no fix until he pays the stolen item to each and every one.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes. It shows that the argument between רבי טרפון and רבי עקיבא is only about a robber, not a buyer. The גמרא is setting up the punch of רב הונא בר יהודה's challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא contrasts the robber with the buyer and never mentions any oath. This makes it sound as if רבי עקיבא is strict on a plain robber just because he robbed. That clashes with Step 6, which said he is strict only after an oath.

keyTerms.meaning: He has no fix (no way to finish his obligation).
He places the value of the stolen item among them.

phrases.english: About what did they disagree?
About one who robbed one of five people,
and does not know from which of them he robbed;
for Rabbi Tarfon says:
he places the value of the stolen item among them and leaves,
and Rabbi Akiva says:
he has no remedy,

phrases.aramaic: עַד שֶׁיְּשַׁלֵּם גְּזֵילָה לְכׇל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד.
phrases.english: until he pays the stolen item to each and every one.

steps.triggerLanguage: עַל מָה נֶחְלְקוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא started in Step 10, moving from the agreed buyer case to the disputed robber case.
steps.raayaObject: That the dispute between רבי טרפון and רבי עקיבא is about a robber as opposed to a buyer, with no mention of an oath.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, brought by רב הונא בר יהודה.

steps.title: If it were about an oath, buying and robbing would be the same
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בר יהודה completes his challenge. If רבי עקיבא is strict only because of a false oath, it should not matter whether the man bought or robbed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you think רבי עקיבא's ruling is about someone who swore falsely, what difference does it make whether he bought or robbed?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes רב הונא בר יהודה's attack on the idea that רבי עקיבא's strict rule is about a robber who swore.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said רבי עקיבא agrees to be lenient with a buyer and is strict only with a robber. A false oath is the same sin whether you bought or robbed. So if the oath were the reason for being strict, the buyer who swore should be treated the same way, and the ברייתא's split between buying and robbing makes no sense.

keyTerms.meaning: And if it enters your mind (if you think that...)
He swore (here: a false oath denying the debt)

phrases.english: And if it enters your mind that it is where he swore,
phrases.notes: He means: if you think רבי עקיבא is strict only with someone who swore falsely.

phrases.aramaic: מָה לִי לָקַח מָה לִי גָּזַל?
phrases.english: what difference is it to me whether he bought, what difference whether he robbed?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ דְּאִישְׁתְּבַע, מָה לִי לָקַח מָה לִי גָּזַל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the ברייתא quoted in steps 10-11 and turns it into a challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer in step 6 that רבי עקיבא's strict rule is about a robber who swore.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A false oath is the same whether the money came from buying or robbing. The ברייתא treats them differently, so the oath cannot be what makes רבי עקיבא strict.

steps.title: רבא's story of the pious man who bought from one of two people
steps.stepSummary: רבא brings another challenge: a story of a חסיד who bought from one of two people and did not know which. רבי טרפון was lenient, and רבי עקיבא required him to pay both.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא raises another objection: There was a story with a pious man who bought from one of two people and did not know which one. He came before רבי טרפון, who told him: Put the payment between them and walk away. He came before רבי עקיבא, who told him: You have no fix until you pay each one of them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא brings a story as a second challenge. This step lays out the story, and the next step will show why it causes a problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this story רבי עקיבא is strict even with a buyer, not only a robber. The key detail is that the man was a חסיד, a pious person. The גמרא will use that detail in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: A pious person, someone who goes beyond the letter of the law
A fix, a way to repair the situation

phrases.english: And Rava raises another objection:
There was a story with a certain pious man
who bought from one of two people

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא הָיָה יוֹדֵעַ מֵאֵיזֶה מֵהֶן לָקַח,
phrases.english: and he did not know from which of them he bought,
and he came before Rabbi Tarfon,

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ: הַנַּח דְּמֵי מִקָּחֲךָ בֵּינֵיהֶם,
phrases.english: he said to him: Put the money for your purchase between them,
and walk away.
He came before Rabbi Akiva,
he said to him: You have no fix,
until you pay each and every one.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעוֹד מֵתִיב רָבָא: מַעֲשֶׂה בְּחָסִיד אֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second, separate source against the same answer from step 6.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי עקיבא is strict even without a false oath.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A story about a pious man brought before רבי טרפון and רבי עקיבא.

steps.title: A pious man would not swear falsely
steps.stepSummary: If רבי עקיבא is strict only with someone who swore falsely, the story makes no sense, because a חסיד would never swear a lie.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you think רבי עקיבא's ruling is about someone who swore, would a pious man swear falsely?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא makes his point from the story. רבי עקיבא was strict with a pious man, and a pious man surely did not swear falsely.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So in the story there was no false oath, yet רבי עקיבא still required paying both people. That shows רבי עקיבא's strict rule does not depend on an oath, which knocks down the answer from step 6.

phrases.english: And if it enters your mind that it is where he swore,
does a pious man swear falsely?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ דְּמִישְׁתְּבַע, חָסִיד מִי מִישְׁתְּבַע בְּשִׁיקְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the story from step 13 to attack the answer in step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי עקיבא's strict rule applies only where the man swore falsely.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The man in the story was a חסיד, so he did not swear falsely. רבי עקיבא was still strict, so his rule cannot depend on an oath.

steps.title: Maybe he swore first and became pious later? No
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the man may have sworn falsely and only later become pious. It rejects this: the 'pious man' in these stories was always one of two sages who were pious from the start.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say he swore and later became pious, there is a rule that wherever we say 'a story with a certain pious man,' it means either רבי יהודה בן בבא or רבי יהודה ברבי אילעאי, and both of them were pious from the beginning!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to save the answer by suggesting the man swore before he became pious, then shuts that idea down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a known tradition about who the 'pious man' in these stories is: always one of two specific sages. Both were pious all their lives, so neither ever swore falsely. רבא's challenge still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you would say (introduces a suggested answer)

phrases.english: And if you would say that he swore
and afterward became a pious man,
but isn't it so that anywhere we say
'a story with a certain pious man' —
it is either Rabbi Yehuda ben Bava,
or Rabbi Yehuda son of Rabbi Elai;

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בָּבָא וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה בְּרַבִּי אִילְעַאי
phrases.english: and Rabbi Yehuda ben Bava and Rabbi Yehuda son of Rabbi Elai
were pious from the beginning!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא דְּמִישְׁתְּבַע וַהֲדַר הָוֵי חָסִיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a possible way out of רבא's challenge in step 14 and immediately rejects it.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggested defense that the man swore falsely before becoming pious.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Tradition says the 'pious man' is always one of two sages who were pious their whole lives, so he never swore falsely.

steps.title: New approach: our משנה follows רבי טרפון
steps.stepSummary: Since the challenges stand, the גמרא changes course. Our משנה (a robber who swore must pay the owner) follows רבי טרפון, who agrees to be strict when the robber swore.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the משנה really follows רבי טרפון, and רבי טרפון agrees in a case where he swore.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops its earlier idea about רבי עקיבא and gives a new explanation of our משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before, the גמרא said our משנה follows רבי עקיבא and that רבי עקיבא is strict only after an oath. Now it says our משנה follows רבי טרפון. רבי טרפון is lenient in general, but he agrees to be strict when the robber swore falsely, which is exactly the case of our משנה.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי טרפון did not change his opinion. He is still lenient with a robber who did not swear. He is strict only where there was a false oath.

phrases.english: Rather, it really follows Rabbi Tarfon,
phrases.notes: 'It' means our משנה here, about a robber who swore falsely and must return the money to the owner.

phrases.english: and Rabbi Tarfon agrees where he swore.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לְעוֹלָם רַבִּי טַרְפוֹן הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected approach after the challenges in steps 12-15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigns the משנה to a different תנא with a narrower agreement.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Our משנה follows רבי עקיבא, who is strict only when the robber swore.
steps.terutzMaskana: Our משנה follows רבי טרפון, who agrees to be strict when the robber swore falsely.

steps.title: The source: the פסוק about returning on the day of guilt
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives רבי טרפון's reason: the פסוק requires the swearer to give the money to the one it belongs to.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? Because the פסוק says: 'To the one it belongs to, he shall give it, on the day of his guilt.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רבי טרפון agrees to be strict after a false oath by quoting a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This פסוק is said about a person who swore falsely to deny money he owed. It requires that the money actually reach the true owner. So after a false oath, putting the money down among the possible owners is not enough.

keyTerms.meaning: His guilt (when he admits guilt and brings his אשם)

phrases.english: What is the reason?
Because the verse says:
"To the one to whom it belongs, he shall give it, on the day of his guilt."

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא? דְּאָמַר קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason behind the new approach in step 16.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי טרפון is strict when the robber swore falsely.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ויקרא 5:24, said about someone who swore falsely about money.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא is strict even without an oath, as a penalty
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא, who requires paying everyone even without an oath, does so because the רבנן penalize the robber.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי עקיבא, who said he must pay everyone even though he did not swear, holds that we penalize him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains רבי עקיבא's view so that it fits with the new approach.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק itself is only about someone who swore. רבי עקיבא is strict even without an oath because of a קנס, a penalty the רבנן added for the robber. This also explains the pious man's story, where there was no oath and רבי עקיבא was still strict.
steps.whatToRemember: Everyone agrees that a robber who swore falsely must make sure the real owner gets paid, because of the פסוק. רבי טרפון is lenient without an oath. רבי עקיבא is strict even without an oath, as a קנס. Our משנה follows רבי טרפון.
steps.whyThisMatters: It separates two reasons for being strict: a Torah requirement after a false oath, and a rabbinic penalty without an oath.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Akiva, who said
even though he did not swear —
penalizes.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא דְּאָמַר אַף עַל גַּב דְּלָא מִישְׁתְּבַע קָנֵיס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the new approach by explaining רבי עקיבא's position.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The פסוק requires full return only after a false oath. רבי עקיבא's strictness without an oath is a rabbinic קנס.

steps.title: Why does the משנה mention an oath at all?
steps.stepSummary: If our משנה follows רבי טרפון, the word 'and he swore' seems unnecessary. A robber who swore must also have admitted, and admitting alone is already enough for רבי טרפון to be strict.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to רבי טרפון: any case where the robber swore must also be a case where he admitted. So why does the משנה specifically say 'and he swore'? Even without an oath he should have to pay!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer from Step 16, that our משנה follows רבי טרפון. It argues that the oath in the משנה adds nothing under רבי טרפון's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A robber who swore falsely only becomes liable for the extra fifth and the קרבן once he admits his lie, so a 'swearing' case always includes an admission. רבי טרפון is strict whenever the robber admits on his own, even with no oath at all. That makes the משנה's words 'and he swore' seem pointless.

keyTerms.meaning: After all; since it is already clear that
It is impossible without; it must be that
Why specifically this case? (asks why a detail was mentioned)

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying the robber never swore. It is asking why the משנה needed to mention the oath, if under רבי טרפון the admission alone is what makes him liable.

phrases.english: And according to Rabbi Tarfon,
after all, wherever he swore,
it must also be that he admitted;
why specifically say "and he swore"?
Even without an oath, too, he should have to pay!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי אִירְיָא ״וְנִשְׁבַּע״? אֲפִילּוּ בְּלָא שְׁבוּעָה נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the claim from Step 16 that our משנה follows רבי טרפון.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that our משנה, which mentions an oath, follows רבי טרפון.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A swearing case always includes an admission, and an admission alone already makes רבי טרפון strict. So the oath detail in the משנה is unnecessary under his view.

steps.title: A ברייתא: רבי טרפון agrees when the robber admits on his own
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that רבי טרפון is strict even without an oath: if a robber tells two people 'I robbed one of you and don't know which,' he must pay each of them.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: רבי טרפון agrees that if someone says to two people, 'I robbed one of you of a מנה and I don't know which of you,' he gives a מנה to this one and a מנה to that one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to prove the claim it just made in Step 19, that רבי טרפון is strict even when there was no oath. The ברייתא continues, with its reason, on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this case there is no oath at all, only the robber coming forward himself. Yet רבי טרפון still requires him to pay both people in full. That supports the challenge: under רבי טרפון, admitting on his own is enough, so the oath in our משנה adds nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: A sum of one hundred דינרים

steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא sets the limit of רבי טרפון's leniency. He is lenient only when the robber does not come forward by himself, and that is what makes the oath in our משנה look unneeded.

phrases.english: As it is taught: Rabbi Tarfon concedes
in the case of one who says to two people:
"I robbed one of you of a maneh,
phrases.notes: A מנה is one hundred דינרים.

phrases.english: and I do not know which of you it was":
he gives this one a maneh and that one a maneh,

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא, מוֹדֶה רַבִּי טַרְפוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source behind the challenge in Step 19.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי טרפון is strict even without an oath when the robber admits on his own.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא in which רבי טרפון agrees that a robber who tells two people he robbed one of them must pay both.
